seoTitle: Ancona cruise port guide: berth 15, Duomo and old port
seoDescription: Ancona cruise ships dock at berth 15, 500 m from the historic centre. City bus €1.60 for 60 min (2026), Duomo open from 08:00, station 15 min on foot.
quickAnswer: Cruise ships dock alongside at berth 15, which the port authority describes as at the gates of the centre; MedCruise puts the centre 500 m from the port, so you walk into town. No shuttle into the city for passengers in transit was confirmed. Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard, and start down from the Duomo at least 75 minutes before.
intro: Ancona is a working ferry port first and a cruise port second. Cruise ships use berth 15 in the old harbour, which the port authority describes as at the gates of the centre, and the berth is shared in summer with ferry traffic. Trajan's Arch stands on the quay, the Duomo of San Ciriaco sits on Guasco hill above, and Vanvitelli's pentagonal Mole is set in the water nearby. The passenger building at berth 15 is a temporary structure; a new 1,600 m² terminal is planned but was still at feasibility-check stage in January 2026. Ancona had 45 cruise calls scheduled for 2026, with MSC Lirica calling every Friday from 3 April to 23 October; MedCruise gives its regular 2026 Friday call as 14:00 to 20:30.

terminals.name: Cruise berth 15 (Banchina Giovanni Da Chio, Molo XXIX Settembre)
terminals.notes: The port authority describes berth 15 as at the gates of the centre. MedCruise, the Mediterranean cruise ports association, lists the distance from the Port of Ancona to the city centre as 500 m and says the historic centre is a few steps from the cruise terminal. Passenger facilities at berth 15 are temporary; the port authority's new 1,600 m² terminal (about €7.2 million) was still being checked at feasibility stage in January 2026. On MSC Lirica's first 2026 call, disembarking passengers left through a purpose-built gate behind the Banca d'Italia building and walked into town. MSC embarkation guests enter through Gate 2A, following signs for 'Traghetti'; MSC's free shuttle links the Biglietteria Marittima on Via Einaudi with the terminal for embarking and disembarking guests, not the city.

walkability.detail: The berth faces the historic centre. Ancona Tourism says that if you arrive from the port you are already in the centre and can visit it on foot, and MedCruise gives 500 m from the port to the city centre. No official walking time in minutes is published, and the exact route depends on the gate your ship uses. The Duomo is on Guasco hill above the port; MSC calls the walk up a stiff climb from the port area.

transportSections.time: The centre is about 500 m from the port (MedCruise); no official walking time published
transportSections.detail: Leave by the gate your ship names in its daily programme and walk into the centre. Santa Maria della Piazza is opposite the port exit; Trajan's Arch and the Clementine Arch are on the old harbour. Wear shoes with grip for the climb to the Duomo.

transportSections.mode: Walk to Ancona Centrale railway station
transportSections.detail: Only needed if you plan a train trip. Taxis and city buses also link the station and the port.

transportSections.cost: €1.60 for 60 min or €1.80 for 100 min bought before boarding; €2.00 from the on-board machine; €3.60 from the driver; €5.00 for 24 h (fares from 1 August 2026)
transportSections.detail: Buy from resellers or online before you board; buying from the driver costs more than double. Validate the ticket when you board. Useful mainly for the Passetto on the far side of the city.
Useful for the climb to the Duomo or for the Passetto. Check the meter is running; Wikivoyage notes reports of overcharging.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard. Start down from the Duomo at least 75 minutes before all-aboard, and leave Ancona Centrale station at least 75 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: No official walking time from the centre to berth 15 is published, so do not cut the return fine. The Duomo is up a steep hill, so allow for the descent. MSC puts the station about 15 minutes on foot from the port. Ancona is a busy ferry port: use the gate named in your daily programme and allow extra time on heavy ferry days.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi straight to the port gate. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme at once.

excursionAdvice: Ancona's own sights are walkable, so the city needs no tour. Loreto is on the railway south of Ancona, but this guide could not confirm train times or fares from Trenitalia; if you go on your own, check the return train on trenitalia.com before you leave and treat the ship's tour as the safer choice on a short or afternoon-only call. The ship's tour earns its price for the Frasassi Caves, Urbino or the Conero coast, which are awkward by public transport on a cruise timetable.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30. MSC Lirica's regular 2026 Friday calls run from 14:00 to 20:30 (MedCruise); on an afternoon call, keep to the old harbour and the Duomo.

steps.what: Walk ashore to Santa Maria della Piazza, then along the old harbour to Trajan's Arch and the Clementine Arch.
Climb Guasco hill to the Duomo of San Ciriaco, open from 08:00.
Walk on to Parco del Cardeto for the clifftop views and old lighthouses.
Walk down to the Loggia dei Mercanti and Piazza del Plebiscito.
Lunch in the centre: stockfish or brodetto.
Walk to the Mole Vanvitelliana and check what is on at the Omero museum or exhibitions.
Coffee near the port, then walk back to the gate named in your daily programme.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Duomo of San Ciriaco
sights.why: Cathedral on Guasco hill, on the site of the acropolis of ancient Ankon, with views over the port and coast.
sights.cost: No entry fee listed by Ancona Tourism
sights.tip: Open 08:00–19:00 daily from 30 May to 26 September; winter weekdays 08:00–18:00 with midday breaks at weekends. Avoid service times.

sights.name: Trajan's Arch
sights.why: Roman arch on the old harbour quay below Guasco hill, where the city's history began.
sights.tip: On the way from the port towards the Duomo.

sights.name: Clementine Arch and the old harbour
sights.why: 18th-century Istrian-stone city gate designed by Vanvitelli, near 14th-century harbour walls.

sights.name: Mole Vanvitelliana
sights.why: Pentagonal building in the harbour, built 1733–1743 to Vanvitelli's design to quarantine visitors, store goods and defend the port. It now houses the Omero tactile museum and exhibitions.
sights.cost: Free to walk round; exhibitions may charge
sights.tip: Check what is on before you go; the walkways are visited by reservation.

sights.name: Santa Maria della Piazza and the Loggia dei Mercanti
sights.why: A Romanesque church directly opposite the port exit, and the 15th-century merchants' loggia with a facade by Giorgio Orsini da Sebenico.
sights.tip: The first stops after you leave the port.

sights.name: Parco del Cardeto
sights.why: Clifftop park high above the sea with lighthouses, bastions, forts and viewpoints.
sights.tip: Paths are mostly unpaved; wear proper shoes.

sights.name: Passetto
sights.why: Ancona's town beach below the cliffs, with more than 500 caves dug by fishermen to keep boats and tools.
sights.tip: It is on the Adriatic side of the city, not by the port. Reach the beach by the stairs or the lift.

sights.name: Sanctuary of the Holy House, Loreto
sights.why: One of Italy's main Marian shrines, in a hilltop town 20 km south of Ancona.
sights.tip: Open 06:15–19:00 from April to September and 06:45–19:00 from October to March. Train times and fares were not confirmed for this guide; check trenitalia.com or take the ship's tour.

beaches.name: Passetto
beaches.howToGetThere: City bus or taxi across the city, then the stairs or lift down to the beach
beaches.note: Rocks and fishermen's caves rather than sand.

beaches.name: Portonovo
beaches.howToGetThere: Ship tour or taxi; Trenitalia also sells a seasonal train-and-bus Conero Link
beaches.cost: Taxi fare or Conero Link ticket
beaches.note: Bay on the Conero coast south of Ancona; allow at least half a day.

commonMistakes.mistake: Underestimating the climb to the Duomo.
commonMistakes.fix: Do it first while it is cool, and start down at least 75 minutes before all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning a full day on an afternoon-only call.
commonMistakes.fix: MSC Lirica's regular 2026 Friday calls arrive at 14:00. Keep to the old harbour and the Duomo.

commonMistakes.mistake: Waiting for a shuttle into town.
commonMistakes.fix: The MSC shuttle on Via Einaudi runs between the ticket office and the terminal. For the city, walk.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying the bus ticket from the driver.
commonMistakes.fix: It costs €3.60 against €1.60 bought beforehand (2026). Buy from a reseller or online.

commonMistakes.mistake: Going to Loreto without checking the return train.
commonMistakes.fix: Check times on trenitalia.com before you leave Ancona, or take the ship's tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Returning to the wrong port gate.
commonMistakes.fix: Ancona is a busy ferry port. Use the gate given in your ship's daily programme.

safety: Wikivoyage describes the Marche as one of Italy's safest regions, and the centre is fine to walk. Take care in the port area, which is busy with ferry traffic, lorries and cars in summer, and stay on marked walkways. The road up Guasco hill and the paths in Parco del Cardeto are steep and uneven. Check taxi meters are running.
scams: Taxis not running the meter; insist it is switched on or agree the fare first.
accessibility: The harbour front is fairly level, but Ancona is a hilly city: the Duomo and the Cardeto park involve steep slopes. Wheelchair users should take a taxi up to the Duomo. The Passetto beach has a lift as well as stairs. The Omero museum at the Mole is a tactile museum designed for visitors with sight loss.
rainyDay: Visit the Duomo, Santa Maria della Piazza and the Omero museum or any exhibition at the Mole Vanvitelliana, then a long lunch in the centre. Cardeto park paths are unpaved and best skipped in rain.
crowdTips: Ancona sees relatively few cruise calls (45 scheduled in 2026), but in summer the old harbour is busy with ferries and berth 15 is shared with ferry passengers. Leave the port promptly after docking and allow extra time to re-enter on busy ferry days. The Duomo is quietest early in the morning.

faqs.q: Is Ancona walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Berth 15 faces the historic centre, which MedCruise puts 500 m from the port. Expect a steep climb if you go up to the Duomo.
No. Cruise ships dock alongside at berth 15.

faqs.q: Is there a shuttle from Ancona cruise port to the city centre?
faqs.a: No shuttle into town was confirmed for this guide. MSC's free shuttle links the Biglietteria Marittima on Via Einaudi with the terminal for embarking and disembarking guests. Walk into the centre.

faqs.q: How far is Ancona train station from the cruise port?
faqs.a: MSC Cruises puts Ancona Centrale about 15 minutes' walk from the port. Taxis and city buses also run between them.

faqs.q: What can I do in Ancona in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk to Santa Maria della Piazza, Trajan's Arch and up to the Duomo, on to Parco del Cardeto, then down to the Loggia dei Mercanti and the Mole Vanvitelliana.
The Passetto is a rocky town beach on the city's Adriatic side, reached by bus or taxi. Portonovo on the Conero coast is best reached by a ship tour or taxi.

faqs.q: How much is the bus in Ancona?
faqs.a: From 1 August 2026 a 60-minute Conerobus ticket is €1.60 bought beforehand, €2.00 from the on-board machine and €3.60 from the driver.
Yes. Take normal care with bags and with traffic in the busy port area.
